en: Itivuttaka 45 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. This discourse was spoken by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Having understood the meaning, the Venerable Ānanda spoke thus: “Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a slayer and the person who is a non-slayer. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, it is well said. Indeed, Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a slayer and the person who is a non-slayer. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a slayer is inferior, the person who is a non-slayer is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a slayer, having slain, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a non-slayer, having not slain, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are non-killers. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a thief and the person who is a non-thief. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a thief is inferior, the person who is a non-thief is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a thief, having stolen, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a non-thief, having not stolen, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are non-thieves. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a speaker of falsehood and the person who is a speaker of truth. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a speaker of falsehood is inferior, the person who is a speaker of truth is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a speaker of falsehood, having spoken falsely, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a speaker of truth, having spoken truly, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are speakers of truth. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a malicious person and the person who is a person of loving-kindness. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a malicious person is inferior, the person who is a person of loving-kindness is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a malicious person, having harbored malice, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a person of loving-kindness, having harbored loving-kindness, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons of loving-kindness. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a divisive person and the person who is a unifying person. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a divisive person is inferior, the person who is a unifying person is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a divisive person, having divided others, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a unifying person, having united others, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are unifiers. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a harsh-speaker and the person who is a gentle-speaker. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a harsh-speaker is inferior, the person who is a gentle-speaker is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a harsh-speaker, having spoken harshly, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a gentle-speaker, having spoken gently, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are gentle-speakers. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a frivolous talker and the person who is a non-frivolous talker. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a frivolous talker is inferior, the person who is a non-frivolous talker is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a frivolous talker, having engaged in frivolous talk, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a non-frivolous talker, having refrained from frivolous talk, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are non-frivolous talkers. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a covetous person and the person who is a non-covetous person. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a covetous person is inferior, the person who is a non-covetous person is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a covetous person, having been covetous, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a non-covetous person, having been non-covetous, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are non-covetous. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a person of ill-will and the person who is a person of good-will. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a person of ill-will is inferior, the person who is a person of good-will is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a person of ill-will, having harbored ill-will, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a person of good-will, having harbored good-will, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons of good-will. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a wrong-viewed person and the person who is a right-viewed person. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a wrong-viewed person is inferior, the person who is a right-viewed person is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a wrong-viewed person, having held wrong views, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a right-viewed person, having held right views, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall become persons who are right-viewed. [The Blessed One said: “Ānanda, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a person of evil conduct and the person who is a person of virtuous conduct. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Of these two, Ānanda, the person who is a person of evil conduct is inferior, the person who is a person of virtuous conduct is superior. Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the person who is a person of evil conduct, having acted with evil conduct, will experience suffering for a long time; the person who is a person of virtuous conduct, having acted with virtuous conduct, will experience happiness for a long time. Therefore
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Monks, dwell delighting in seclusion, rejoicing in seclusion, devoted to internal tranquility of mind, not neglecting jhāna, endowed with insight, and frequenters of empty huts."
For those who dwell delighting in seclusion, who take pleasure in seclusion, who are devoted to internal tranquility of mind, who have not cast off the jhānas,

who are endowed with insight, and who cultivate empty huts, one of two fruits is to be expected: either final knowledge in this very life or, if there is a residue remaining, the state of non-returning.
“Full knowledge in this very life, or, if there is a residue of clinging, the state of a non-returner.
This is what the Blessed One said.
“Those whose minds are peaceful, who are prudent,
clearly see the Dhamma with right insight.”
Those who are indifferent toward sensual pleasures,
“Unfit for decline, they are in the very presence of Nibbāna.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
